scope: Verified native cloud CPU-compositor optional mode; lightweight 4x4 offscreen HDR capability/readback only; no world attempted
rerun_rule: Choose a NEW nonexistent run directory; never reuse this completed run. For separately released full-world scope select outer1320 before launch, preflight-first, then navigate only after visible viewport/capability gates. Deadline includes setup and cleanup.
viewport_procedure: Fresh window auto-normalized to1188x848; moved/resized through normal native UI to1288x891, reloaded, then visibly verified1280x800/DPR1. Never resize after scene scheduler starts.

cleanup.method: Alt+F4 in specifically owned native CPU preflight window

limitations: Ownership covers the fresh root process group plus descendants observed while ancestry was verifiable.
A child that detaches/reparents before observation can escape attribution. Unobserved detached processes are not proven absent.
RSS is a sampled sum (shared pages can be counted repeatedly); this is not a cgroup hard cap and between-poll peaks can be missed.
PID start ticks and pidfds prevent signaling a replacement PID. Inaccessible or ambiguous identities are not signaled.
Monotonic deadlines bound monitor waits; OS scheduling stalls or blocked kernel/filesystem operations cannot be bounded by Python.
SIGKILL or interpreter/host failure can prevent cleanup; keep the monitor Terminal alive and cancel with Ctrl+C or the CANCEL file.
No claim of browser sandbox audit, scene completion, GPU completion, or visual/performance acceptance follows from this process log.

HDR4x test clears a tiny framebuffer and resolves/readbacks it; it does not run scene shaders or prove world rendering, fence completion, quality or realtime performance. CPU-compositor selection is in requested argv; internal compositor architecture was not separately inspected.
path_redaction: Checkout prefix replaced with <checkout> for publication; original exact command and raw run evidence retained locally in ignored backups. Recorded source hashes still identify the code used at the original launch.
